newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit off high, but in range on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit off high, but in range on profit-taking.

text.p: The ringgit continued to be under pressure from profit-taking in late Asian trading after slipping from a four-month high overnight, dealers said.
But the Malaysian currency stayed in a narrow range until Europe opened. At 0800 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.5010/15 a ringgit after hitting 2.4940/50 overnight.
The dealers said rumours of Bank Negara intervention overnight put a stop to the ringgit's rise, which was mainly speculative trading.
"Everybody seems to have jumped on to the dollar/ringgit bandwagon," said a dealer with a Singapore-based European bank.
He said what started as ringgit/Singapore dollar operation early on Monday had turned into a bull run for the ringgit.
"The profit-taking is mainly out of Kuala Lumpur," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank, adding that further gains for the ringgit were possible once the profit-taking ended.
Dealers said higher interest rates in Malaysia, a sharply improved trade balance figure, and movement from Sing to ringgit was helping the Malaysian unit.
They said Singaporeans who had maintained long Singapore dollar positions ahead of the city-state's elections on January 2 were returning to other currencies, particularly the ringgit.
